findings.description: The scratch-repository helper passes `-c protocol.file.allow=always` to every git invocation. This switches off the file-transport restriction Git added for CVE-2022-39253 (submodule clones from local paths). In the shown hunks the helper is only defined, so it is not yet clear which fixtures depend on it; if any fixture ever clones or updates a submodule from a path it did not create itself, the protection is gone for that operation.
findings.failure_mode: A fixture that clones a repository containing a .gitmodules pointing at a local path would follow it, which the default `protocol.file.allow=user` would refuse.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the override unless a specific fixture needs it; if one does, pass it only on that call rather than in the shared wrapper, and add a comment naming the fixture.

findings.description: Ownership of a leftover `sprint-comp-<n>` directory is proven by a marker file `.sprint-comp-<n>.owner` in the shared a2a directory inside the checkout. Any local writer of that directory can create such a marker with a `where` line copied from this host and a dead pid, and the next teardown will recursively delete `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-comp-<n>` and any `.reap-*` siblings. The naming convention makes a real sprint collision unlikely, and the deletion requires write access the attacker already holds, so impact is confined to confusing or destroying test artefacts.
findings.failure_mode: A planted marker causes the suite's teardown to delete a directory it did not create.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the owner's start token (already computed by _sweep_start) in the marker and require it to match the dead pid's recorded token, or restrict the sweep to directories whose inode was recorded in the marker at setup.

findings.description: The `errlog` stub arm emits `sk-ant-api03-SECRETSECRETSECRETSECRET1234`, a string in the real Anthropic key format, and CMP-13 exports `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-presence-only-never-printed` without the leak assertions that CMP-4 and CMP-6 apply. Both values are obvious canaries, but the committed key-shaped literal is the kind of string that repository secret scanners flag, and CMP-13 leaves one credential path unasserted.
findings.failure_mode: Secret-scanning tooling raises a false positive on the committed fixture; a regression that prints the key in the CMP-13 path would go unnoticed because that test does not check stdout or stderr for the canary.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the key-shaped canary (it is needed to exercise the mask) but build it at runtime from parts, and add the same `[[ "$result" != *canary* ]]` and stderr assertions to CMP-13 that CMP-6 already has.
